From the sidebar:

Please keep your idea short, if possible, narrow it down to one sentence. Anything longer than that will likely go unnoticed.

Excellent writeup and I really support most of the ideas.

User User control and self-moderation

I see it simply as a menu under user's settings.

On Topic +10_________X__________-10 Spam
Constructive +10_____X______________-10 Destructive
Original +10_____X______________-10 Repost

Each user adjusts their own slidebars according to personal preference. If I want to see more OC I simply slide the bar in that direction. Posts are ranked by user submitted tags. For example when you tag something as a repost its repost score goes -1. If I have set my repost bar to -3 I will stop seeing that post once it reaches -3. No need for censorship.

Hashtags

I do believe user categorized data is more valuable than bot categorized data so I support hashtags. The important bit here is to implement hashtags in such a way as to minimize clutter. Any user should be able to completely turn them of in their UI. Selective enabling of hashtags should also be possible.

True Anonymity

It may be incompatible with a karma system. In other word if you offer true anonymity and non-anonymity at the same time the users may gravitate to one extreme and this may create social pressure against using the other. I like anonymity but I'm undecided on this one.

Ephemerality

Not a big fan of this one. More and more human communication happens online but much of that is lost due to ephemerality. Please read the mission statement of archive.org where they explain why they collect and store pages from the internet. A social platform is significant because it shows how the humanity experience history as it happens. This must be kept alive and not lost.

User Democracy

Instead of voting for mods why don't we just subscribe to them? This way anyone can become a mod to any sub. Also any user can choose to subscribe or unsubscribe to any mod. For example lets suppose we have a mod list like this:

Moderator Comment Subverse Actions
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/mod/Kiwikku (I mod r/blackout2015) v/blackout2015 Delete[X] Ban [X] Promote[ ] Tags[X]

/bot/RepostRemover (Removes all reposts!!) v/all Delete[X] Ban [ ] Promote[ ] Tags[X]

Notice how I have subscribed to some actions of some mods but not to their other actions. If some mod starts power tripping in the future I simply unsubscribe completely and I'm done. No drama whatsoever.

Karma On reddit the karma had no fiction except dick measuring. I think further gamification is important and karma can be used to fullfill a function in that regard. Of course there may be need for different kinds of karma. For example different karma for credibility and different for cat picture reposts.

User ownership of data: In a digital world the deletion of data from the internet is completely hypothetical. This is a futile endeavor.

When working with (what I believe to be) unix shell calls, how do you condense multiple into one line? For example, if I had;

prefix_removed=${i#*_}

dashes_removed=${prefix_removed//-/}

suffix_removed=${dashes_removed%.tar}

output=$suffix_removed

How would I do this without assigning a new variable every time?

I'm not too familiar with this but can't you just combine them all like this?

output=${${${i#*_}//-/}%.tar}

EDIT: Nope. Nested substitution is not a bash feature, my bad.

Usually when I edit a multi-line shell command with <Ctrl-x><Ctrl-e> it condenses it into a one-line command and puts that in my shell history. I tried this and it left the four lines as separate history entries. Either that bash feature doesn't handle special cases like this, or there is no way to condense this into one line.

$ # The following is for Bash 4. Not tested with other shells.
$ #
$ i='(system name)_(year)-(month)-(day).tar'
$ [[ "$i" =~ _(.+)\. ]] ; echo -E "${BASH_REMATCH[1]//-/}"
(year)(month)(day)
$
$ condense () { [[ "$1" =~ _(.+)\. ]] ; echo -E "${BASH_REMATCH[1]//-/}" ;}
$
$ output="$( condense '(system name)_(year)-(month)-(day).tar' )"
$ echo -E "$output"
(year)(month)(day)
$ 
$ # HTH :-)
